newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala's Arzu heads to Europe for help in peace.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala's Arzu heads to Europe for help in peace.

text.p: Fresh from having signed a peace agreement to end his country's civil war, Guatemalan President Alvaro Arzu travels to Europe on Friday for a week-long trip aimed at drumming up money to help his country secure its hard-fought peace.

Arzu is slated to meet leaders of Spain, Belgium, Holland and the European Union to promote Guatemala's plans to implement ambitious promises contained in a historic peace treaty signed on Dec. 29 between the government and the leftist Guatemalan National Revolutionary Unit (URNG) rebels.

Guatemala wants more than $1.5 billion in foreign aid and loans for programmes to modernise the state, attack poverty and resettle hundreds of thousands of Guatemalans displaced during 36 years of civil war.

The Central American nation also needs funds for a commission to investigate allegations of rampant human rights violations, mostly attributed to the army during more than three decades of counterinsurgency campaigns.
"The president has a very intense agenda. The meetings are not about protocol, they are work meetings," presidential spokesman Ricardo de la Torre told a news conference.
